Confirms task.description's premise. 2. EXISTING LETFLOW-QUEUE COVERAGE READ AND QUOTED: read c:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow-queue/test/letflow_queue/tasks_test.exs in full. Test 'does not return a task that is already done or blocked' (lines 109-114, describe "get_next_task/1"): registers a task, calls `Tasks.release_lock(t1.id, force: true, status: "done")`, then asserts `assert {:error, :no_eligible_task} = Tasks.get_next_task("agent-1")` -- proving a task with a terminal status (the test exercises "done"; "blocked" is the same code path per the function's status-list exclusion, named identically in the test's own title) is excluded from get_next_task's eligible set. Test 'releasing with status blocked works too' (lines 312-320, describe "release_lock/2"): registers a task, locks it via `Tasks.set_lock(task.id, "agent-1")`, then asserts `assert {:ok, released} = Tasks.release_lock(task.id, agent_id: "agent-1", status: "blocked")` followed by `assert released.status == "blocked"` -- proving release_lock accepts and persists status:"blocked" as a first-class transition, not an error path (contrast with the file's own 'rejects an invalid status value' test at lines 367-372, which asserts `{:error, :invalid_status}` for a bogus value -- "blocked" is not treated that way). Together these two tests cover exactly the mechanical claim this run's documentation now describes as existing fact: status:"blocked" is a valid release_lock transition, and a blocked task is thereafter excluded from get_next_task -- i.e. it does NOT auto-close/re-surface via the queue mechanism the new prose describes. Both tests pass against the current letflow-queue main (they are pre-existing, unmodified by this run). 3. NO NEW TEST WRITTEN: no ExUnit file created or edited in letflow or letflow-queue by this step, per task.description point 4.
